description:
Decouple stream-chunk arrival from rendering. Per-chunk handlers in `OctoPi.TUI.Interactive` become near-no-ops; rendering is driven by a tick.

## Shape

Mirror the `RenderLoop` idle/deadline/drain pattern, but with **append-fold** semantics for stream deltas instead of replace-with-latest:

- Idle at no scheduled tick.
- First `MessageUpdate` since last tick arms a deadline (`tick_ms` from now).
- Subsequent `MessageUpdate`s before the deadline fold into the pending partial without rendering.
- On the deadline, render once and clear the pending state.
- On stream-close, force-flush immediately rather than wait for the deadline.

## Acceptance

- `MessageUpdate` `handle_info` p99 (from telemetry) drops to sub-millisecond regardless of message length.
- `transcript.render` call rate during streaming is bounded by the tick, not the chunk rate.
- `key.latency` p99 during a long streaming response improves vs the baseline captured in opi-4dx.2.
- No visible regression in streaming smoothness in tmux (deltas still appear at perceived real-time pace).

## Notes

- Tick budget is heavier than `RenderLoop`'s 16 ms (it does Markdown work). Likely 30–33 ms; confirm against telemetry.
- Non-text events (tool-call boundaries, message finalize) must stay ordered with deltas. Either route them through the same pending state or flush before handling them.
title: Pull-tick render coalescing in Interactive
